name: Okta: suspend user and revoke sessions
description: Run on a case: looks up the case's user in Okta, suspends the account and revokes all of its Okta sessions and OAuth tokens, then writes a note with each HTTP status.

params.label: Okta domain
params.help: Your Okta org host name, without https://. A custom domain works too.

params.label: API Services app client ID
params.help: Client ID of the Okta API Services app integration (General > Client Credentials).

secrets.name: OKTA_RESPONSE_PRIVATE_KEY
secrets.description: Private key of the Okta API Services app (JWK JSON or PEM). The app needs the Organization Administrator role (or Group Administrator scoped to the groups this may act on); Help Desk Administrator cannot suspend users.

setup:
### Okta side
1. Applications > Create App Integration > **API Services**.
2. General > Client Credentials > Client authentication **Public key / Private key**. Keep **Require Demonstrating Proof of Possession (DPoP) header in token requests** ON. Add key > **Generate new key**, and copy the private key (JSON or PEM) and its `kid`.
3. **Okta API Scopes** > Grant `okta.users.manage` AND `okta.users.read` (the user lookup needs read).
4. **Admin roles** > assign the role: **Organization Administrator** (or Group Administrator scoped to the groups this may act on); Help Desk Administrator cannot suspend users.

### Here
1. Settings > Secrets: add `OKTA_RESPONSE_PRIVATE_KEY` (paste the private key; allowed host = your Okta domain).
2. Install with `OKTA_DOMAIN` and `OKTA_CLIENT_ID`. Paste the private key as a JWK (it includes the `kid`); a PEM key has no `kid`, so also set `key_id` in the auth block of each HTTP step.

### What it does
Target = the case's `username` attribute, else its first `email` artifact. With no target it only writes a note.
1. `GET /api/v1/users/<login>` (accepts an ID, login or unambiguous short name) to get the user ID; not found > note, nothing else.
2. `POST /api/v1/users/<id>/lifecycle/suspend` (only works on ACTIVE users; a 400 means it was not active).
3. `DELETE /api/v1/users/<id>/sessions?oauthTokens=true` (revokes Okta sessions plus OIDC/OAuth tokens; sessions inside downstream apps are not cleared).
4. Note with both HTTP statuses (200 and 204 are success). Undo with `POST /api/v1/users/<id>/lifecycle/unsuspend`.

Docs: [Users lifecycle](https://developer.okta.com/docs/api/openapi/okta-management/management/tag/UserLifecycle/#tag/UserLifecycle/operation/suspendUser), [Revoke user sessions](https://developer.okta.com/docs/api/openapi/okta-management/management/tag/UserSessions/#tag/UserSessions/operation/revokeUserSessions), [Admin roles](https://help.okta.com/oie/en-us/Content/Topics/Security/administrators-admin-comparison.htm).
